scope: Bound root dictionary entry setter staging before caller-owned data is copied or moved into the writer.

behavior: Both const-vector and rvalue setRootDictEntries overloads reject vectors above DRW_Dictionary::kMaxEntries before copying or moving them.
Rejected setter input marks the pending root dictionary state invalid, so writeObjects refuses before emitting bytes rather than serializing stale entries.
The const-vector setter copies into a temporary and swaps only after successful allocation; allocation failure marks input rejected.
A later valid setter call clears the rejection state, allowing corrected same-codec retry.

focused.coverage: ASCII/Binary const-vector and rvalue count refusal before staging, caller/prior-state preservation, no output change, and corrected same-codec retry.

limitations: The 100,000-entry ceiling is an internal resource limit, not a DXF format maximum or support claim.
The selector proves setter admission and failure/retry state; it does not qualify root dictionary serialization semantics or native consumer behavior.
Other staging/assembly paths, allocation-failure injection, rollback after earlier staged records, source lifetime and platform policy remain open.
next: Continue the safety and caller-state audit on the remaining independent staging, assembly and rollback paths.
